hints: Focus on what kind of Period 3 ion has 18 electrons, a cation from the left or an anion from the right?
Remember that Y forms an 18-electron anion like $\text{S}^{2-}$ or $\text{Cl}^{-}$, which has an extra electron shell compared to a 10-electron cation.
Connect the positions to atomic radius, since radius decreases across Period 3 as atomic number increases, so the element on the left is larger.
walkthrough:
**Identify what Y must be**

Y is in Period 3 and its stable ion has 18 electrons. That is the argon configuration.

Only the non-metals on the right form this: $\text{P}^{3-}$, $\text{S}^{2-}$, $\text{Cl}^{-}$

**Use the ionic radius clue to find X**

We are told ion of Y is larger than ion of X. An 18-electron anion has 3 shells (n = 3) and is large due to extra repulsion.

For X to have a smaller ion, X must lose its outer shell to form a 10-electron cation like $\text{Na}^{+}$, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ or $\text{Al}^{3+}$ with only 2 shells.

**Check atomic numbers fit**

This makes perfect sense because X is a metal on the left and Y is a non-metal on the right, so Y has the greater atomic number. X forms a 10-electron ion.

**Compare atomic radii**

Across Period 3, atomic radius decreases left to right because nuclear charge increases and pulls the same shell in more strongly.

$$\text{atomic radius decreases: Na > Mg > Al > Si > P > S > Cl}$$
Since X is to the left of Y, X has the greater atomic radius.

options.A: Correct. X is a left-side metal forming a 10-electron cation ($\text{Na}^{+}$, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, $\text{Al}^{3+}$) which is much smaller than the 18-electron anion of Y. X is also to the left of Y, so X has the larger atomic radius.
options.B: Incorrect about atomic radius. 10 electrons for X is right, but Y cannot have the greater atomic radius. Atomic radius decreases across the period with increasing atomic number, and Y is to the right of X.
options.C: Incorrect about ionic electrons. If both X and Y had 18-electron ions, both would be anions on the right side. Then their ionic sizes would be similar and the radius clue would not give a large difference. The large size difference tells us X is a small 10-electron cation.
options.D: Incorrect on both columns. X cannot have 18 electrons if its ion is much smaller than the 18-electron ion of Y, and Y to the right cannot have the larger atomic radius across Period 3.
